findings.documented: The API key is sent as the ?api_key= query parameter.
findings.actual: The API requires the key in the X-API-Key request header.
findings.how_found: An authenticated collection request using the documented query parameter returned 401 with an instruction to send the key in the X-API-Key header; retrying with that header succeeded.
findings.impact: Client requests must send X-API-Key rather than relying on the documented query parameter.

findings.documented: Login requires email and password in the request body.
findings.actual: Login also requires the X-API-Key request header.
findings.how_found: The first login attempt returned 401 missing X-API-Key header; adding the header made login succeed.
findings.impact: The login client must include the API key even though the login body alone appears sufficient in the documentation.

findings.documented: The response contains token and tokens are valid for 24 hours; there is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: The response uses access_token, includes refresh_token and refresh_url=/auth/refresh, and expires_in is 900 seconds (15 minutes). The /auth/refresh flow accepts refresh_token and returns the same token shape.
findings.how_found: The raw login response was inspected and the refresh endpoint was tested directly.
findings.impact: A frontend must refresh the session during a 30-minute session instead of assuming one login remains valid.

findings.documented: Pagination is page-based and page is incremented starting at 1.
findings.actual: The page parameter is ignored. Offset is the real pagination mechanism.
findings.how_found: Multiple requests with changing page/skip/cursor-like parameters returned the same first window; changing offset returned a genuinely different window.
findings.impact: Using the documented page parameter cannot retrieve the complete dataset.

findings.documented: limit may be requested up to 200 records per page.
findings.actual: The server returns at most 50 records per request, even when limit=200 is requested.
findings.how_found: Requests using limit=200 consistently returned 50-record result windows.

findings.documented: total is the exact number of matching records.
findings.actual: The declared totals undercount the retrievable dataset: listings 3879 vs 4100, rentals 1466 vs 1550, projects 435 vs 460.
findings.how_found: The client was changed to stop only when a genuinely empty offset page was returned rather than trusting total; the final page traversal produced the larger counts.
findings.impact: Trusting total causes incomplete answers; Q1/Q5/Q10 and any full-dataset analysis must use end-of-data pagination.

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property and listing IDs are distinct records.
findings.actual: At least some records represent the same physical property across listing sources; a deterministic clustering pass found 25 multi-record clusters among 4100 listings.
findings.how_found: Clustered listings using rounded latitude/longitude, bedroom count, and carpet area, then manually inspected representative clusters. For example, ZER-4003993 and ZER-4002843 both refer to Sobha Serenity with matching location/bedroom/area characteristics and slightly different prices.
findings.impact: The unique-property answer cannot be obtained by simply counting listing records; cross-source deduplication is required.

findings.documented: The listings endpoint returns active listings only.
findings.actual: The response contains an undocumented is_live field and includes 867 records with is_live=false; 3233 have is_live=true.
findings.how_found: All returned listing objects were inspected for fields and is_live was counted across the full 4100-record dataset.
findings.impact: The frontend cannot assume every /v1/listings record is active; it filters is_live=true for active listings.

findings.documented: Listing records contain physically meaningful price, area, floor, and bedroom values.
findings.actual: 45 listing records contain values that cannot describe a plausible built property, including non-positive prices, floor numbers above total floors, carpet area above super-built-up area, non-positive bedroom counts on non-land records, or implausibly low price-per-square-foot values.
findings.how_found: Applied explicit physical-consistency checks to the complete 4100-record dataset and manually reviewed the resulting candidate set before using it for Q4.
findings.impact: Those 45 records are excluded from the Q6 2-BHK price-per-square-foot calculation and reported as Q4 corrupt listing IDs.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees.
findings.actual: The project price fields are recorded in crores; P40231 has price_max=99.8, which corresponds to ₹998,000,000.
findings.how_found: The full price_max distribution was 1.01/1.46/1.87/2.4/99.8, which is consistent with crore-scale values rather than rupees; the maximum was then converted by 1e7.
findings.impact: Q7 must convert the project price_max value from crores to rupees.

findings.documented: Listing carpet_area and super_built_up_area are measured in square feet.
findings.actual: 326 individual listing records have both area fields at sizes consistent with square metres; converting those records by 10.7639 makes their dimensions plausible. This is a per-record issue, not a source-wide website bug.
findings.how_found: The source-level carpet/super ratios were healthy across all five website prefixes (~0.75-0.76), which disproved a source-wide units hypothesis. A per-record absolute-area check then isolated 326 records.
findings.impact: Area calculations need a per-record units correction before Q4/Q6 analysis.

findings.actual: The documented endpoint and tested method/path variants return 404 Not Found; no server-side favourites endpoint exists at the documented path.
findings.how_found: GET, POST, DELETE and plausible path/method variants were tested directly against the live API.
findings.impact: Saved listings were implemented client-side, keyed by logged-in user email in localStorage, so they still persist across reload and re-login.

findings.actual: The endpoint returns 404 Not Found on the tested path variants.
findings.how_found: Direct GET requests were made against the documented path and plausible variants.
findings.impact: The Insights page computes analytics client-side from the verified listing dataset instead of depending on a dead endpoint.

findings.documented: Timestamps use UTC Z format everywhere.
findings.actual: health.server_time is returned with an explicit +05:30 offset, while listing posted_at values use Z/UTC.
findings.how_found: The health response and listing timestamp samples were inspected directly.
findings.impact: Timestamp parsing should honor the actual offset rather than assuming every endpoint uses the documented Z suffix.

findings.documented: Listing descriptions represent genuine property listings.
findings.actual: Two listing records reuse the exact same description text while being separate listing records with different listing IDs and prices.
findings.how_found: Normalized exact-description matching across all 4100 listings found one description text reused twice; the matching records were DWE-4003375 and 100-4003487.
findings.impact: These two records are reported as the narrow Q9 fake-listing set rather than treating broader shared-phone clusters as automatically fraudulent.
